note: City cores at highest combined flood risk. bbox = [west, south, east, north] in degrees. Built by scripts/build_regions.py at 10 m from USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second; downloaded in the app as region packs.

regions.name: Sacramento
regions.why: Two rivers held back by levees. Natomas and the Pocket sit 15-25 ft below the Sacramento River at flood stage; FEMA maps Natomas A99 (levee still being built to the 1% standard).

regions.name: New Orleans
regions.why: Much of the city is below sea level inside levees and depends on pumps; heavy rain ponds where the pumps can't keep up.

regions.name: Miami & Miami Beach
regions.why: High-tide flooding on sunny days, porous limestone under the seawalls, and hurricane surge.

regions.name: Norfolk
regions.why: The fastest relative sea-level rise on the US East Coast; tidal flooding closes streets many times a year.

regions.name: Charleston
regions.why: The peninsula's low streets flood at king tides and in ordinary heavy rain when the outfalls are under water.

regions.name: Houston
regions.why: Flat land, clay soil and bayous that overtop in heavy rain; Harvey put 50 in of rain on the region.

regions.name: New York City (harbor shore)
regions.why: Lower Manhattan, Red Hook and the south Brooklyn and Queens shore flooded in Sandy; basement apartments flood in cloudbursts.

regions.name: Boston
regions.why: Much of downtown, the Seaport and East Boston is filled marsh a few feet above today's high tides.
